summary.headline: Page Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.9% to INR14,204 mn and PAT fell about 4%, as ~3 days of billing slipped into Q2 on logistics disruption.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 7.9% YoY to INR14,204 mn and volume rose 5.7% to 61.9 mn pieces, but management said quarter-end logistics and manpower disruptions left about three days of billing undelivered. EBITDA fell 1.9% YoY to INR2,890 mn, with margin at 20.3% versus 22.4% a year earlier, as input costs (cotton, nylon, synthetics) spiked from March–May. PAT declined about 4% to INR1,928 mn. Management said most of the delayed billing and the May price increase (about 2.2% weighted average) should show up in Q2, and it reaffirmed double-digit annual volume growth and the 19–21% EBITDA margin range.

segments.name: Jockey innerwear and core range
segments.commentary: Volume growth of 5.7% was ahead of revenue growth of 7.9%-minus-mix, with lower-ASP accessories and socks gaining share due to scheme design. Schemes are now spread across quarters under the ARS model.

segments.name: Groove 3 (street fashion line)
segments.commentary: Launched in June 2026 across close to 500 exclusive brand stores; management said sell-through looks very good.

segments.name: Disney/Marvel character merchandise
segments.commentary: Go-to-market planned for end-June; a large portion of revenue expected in Q2.

segments.name: Speedo
segments.commentary: Multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1 from consolidation in swim offline; online is upwards of 35% of Speedo business. Combined Q4+Q1 view is about 950 stores.

guidance_outlook: Full-year volume growth target remains double-digit, phased across quarters; Q2–Q4 must show above-average volume growth to recover Q1 shortfall (analyst read-through of about 11–12% average).
Majority of the roughly three days of undelivered billing (seven days vs normal three to four) expected to be reported in Q2.
Full benefit of the mid-May price increase to flow through in Q2 under FIFO billing; difference between volume and value growth expected to widen from Q1 levels.
Annual EBITDA margin outlook retained at 19–21%.
Management intends to hold prices and drive volumes if margins stay within 19–21%; another price action possible if input costs re-escalate.
Marketing spend to remain at 4–5% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Management is augmenting in-house manufacturing capacity and investing above plan, alongside outsourced garment supply.
Odisha and K.R. Pet manufacturing facilities are scaling up progressively.
Distribution: 115,871 multi-brand outlets, 1,640 exclusive brand stores, 930 large format stores.
E-commerce: two fulfilment centres (one South, one North); management prefers outright model over marketplace.
Consumer data platform (CDP) expected to go live by end-August 2026, subject to DPDP Act compliance.
DMS rollout: all distributors targeted on DMS by end-2026 or Q1 FY28 at latest.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 5.7% was driven by healthy consumer demand across EBOs, e-commerce and wider retail.
Price increases: about 2.5% in January 2026 (product-quality related, not input-cost linked) and about 2.2% weighted average in mid-May 2026 (input-cost linked).
Input cost inflation in cotton, nylon, synthetic fabrics and packaging peaked in May; prices eased by late June but remain volatile.
Management said the May price increase only partially offsets the raw material escalation.
Pricing is uniform across channels with no flash sales or markdowns; quick commerce is on an outright model.
Secondary growth was better than primary in Q1 because of undelivered billing; tertiary and EBO performance was better than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth below the double-digit target flagged in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was affected by a planned scheme phasing change under ARS and about three days of undelivered billing; the full-year double-digit target is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price increase offset input costs and restore margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The May increase only partially covers input costs; the full benefit flows from Q2 and management said prices have eased below April–May levels, so it is a 'waiting game'.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days fall from 73 to 66?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not intend to reduce inventory further, that Q1 had some lost sales from non-availability, and that inventory is now at an optimum level.

qa_highlights.question: What were the logistics and manpower disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party logistics and labour concerns linked to fuel price rumours, fuel availability and a June SAR drive disrupted last-mile delivery to distributors at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Speedo multi-brand outlets decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline swim consolidation as business moved online; Speedo multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1, and about 950 counting Q4 and Q1 combined.

qa_highlights.question: Why did A&P spend fall 5% in FY26 and is the company shifting to outright e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included a disproportionate World Cup campaign; marketing will stay at 4–5% of revenue. E-commerce has tilted to outright because of quick commerce, and price governance is maintained through partnerships.

risks_watch: Recovery of about three days of undelivered billing and above-average Q2–Q4 volume growth needed for double-digit annual volume target.
Input cost volatility (cotton, nylon, petroleum-based synthetics) and possible re-escalation requiring another price action.

Karnataka minimum wage: garmenting wage hike applied from April; second announcement affecting third-party support staff was withheld in late July; impact on margins from a garment-level hike not quantified.
Logistics and third-party labour reliability at quarter end.
Speedo multi-brand outlet consolidation and channel shift online.
Shift of e-commerce towards outright model and its implications for pricing control.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year volume and margin outlook, but defensive on the Q1 miss, which management attributed to timing and temporary disruptions. Answers on input cost hedging and quantification were hedged ("very difficult to put a number"), and the company did not quantify the Karnataka wage impact.
key_quotes: The underlying demand and volume momentum therefore remained better than what was reported as revenue growth.
So typically, every quarter we have – quarter ending we have about three to four days of billing that does not get delivered and gets pushed to the next quarter.
I think we've reached optimum level of inventory both in the value chain as well as the inventory at Page level.
As long as we're able to operate in that space, I think the intent would be to hold prices and drive volumes.
